correctness.rationale: Complete RESULT.md proof was reconstructed: image U=im A has dimension r, B -> AB surjects onto Hom(F_q^m,U), with uniform fibers q^{m(n-r)}. Writing domain U plus complement, AB block [[C,D],[0,0]], its nilpotence iff uniform C in M_r(F_q) is nilpotent. The classical exact count q^{r^2-r}, proved again using Fitting decomposition and telescoping C_k factors, yields conditional q^{-r}, including r=0. Averaging by the left kernel |ker A^T|=q^{m-r}, with each nonzero y annihilating all n columns at probability q^{-n}, gives the exact rectangular formula. Artin–Wedderburn and componentwise nilpotence give the semisimple product and matrix/extension-field collision. Independent literal enumeration of all pairs in small prime-field rectangular cases confirmed every conditional rank fiber and aggregate probability. Distinguishes matrices over extension fields from naive integers modulo q.
residual_risks: Finite brute-force only covers small prime-field cases; all prime powers and sizes rest on the Fitting and kernel-count proof.
Applies only to finite semisimple unital rings; positive Jacobson radical not covered.

value.rationale: Nilpotent-product probability is a motivated invariant in finite-ring statistics. The exact rectangular conditional law for arbitrary aspect ratio and field is a reusable ingredient and exhibits unexpected simple symmetry. The semisimple formula reveals that matrix algebras and extension fields cannot be distinguished by this single statistic, a precise limitation on ring recognition. This goes beyond restating the single-operator nilpotent count.
residual_risks: Semisimple multiplicativity alone is elementary once full matrix factors are known; it is not counted as an independent deep theorem.

final_claim: For independent uniform A in M_{m x n}(F_q), B in M_{n x m}(F_q), P(AB nilpotent)=q^{-m}+q^{-n}-q^{-(m+n)} for all m,n>=1 and prime powers q. For fixed rank-r A, exactly q^{mn-r} choices B succeed. Semisimple unital R=product_i M_{d_i}(F_{q_i}) has nilpotent-product probability product_i(2 q_i^{-d_i}-q_i^{-2d_i}), equal factorwise to field F_{q_i^{d_i}}.
